title: Spectator Autoscaler and Tenant Fallback Playbook (PRD notes)
body:
Summary:

This doc captures the Spectator Autoscaler concept and a practical tenant-fallback playbook for Dedicated capacity. The idea: run a low-cost observer (the "Spectator") that continuously evaluates pool health, tenant demand signals, and cross-pool slack to make conservative, reversible suggestions for short-term soft increases (micro-bursts), enforceable soft-isolation lanes, and controlled fallbacks.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Customers buy Dedicated pools to guarantee throughput and latency, but demand spikes and seasonality cause tension between over-provisioning (waste) and under-provisioning (SLO breaches).
- Current heavy-handed prewarming / reserved capacity workflows are slow and opaque to tenants. We need an ops-light mechanism that:
  * Maintains tenant isolation guarantees for committed capacity
  * Enables safe, observable micro-bursts to absorb transient spikes
  * Provides deterministic fallback semantics when capacity is constrained
  * Minimizes accounting surprises for billing and incident owners

Key concepts (new vocabulary):
- Spectator: a read-only analytics agent that watches metrics at pool, host, and tenant granularity. It does not change orchestration state directly, but emits proposals to the Autoscale Broker.
- Autoscale Broker: authoritative controller that can enact soft-burst leases, create ephemeral lanes, and trigger fallback contracts.
- Soft-burst lease: a short-lived (minutes to hours) temporary increase in a tenant's soft quota. Conservatively priced and revokable.
- Spectator Lane: a special, low-priority lane where certain best-effort workloads can run when pool slack exists. Isolated from committed lanes by QoS fencing.
- Fallback Contract: a deterministic downgrade policy when capacity saturates—e.g., model-variant fallback, degraded throughput, or queued request shaping.

Goals / success metrics:
- Reduce number of SLO incidents for committed tenants experiencing short spikes by 40% in pilot pools.
- Keep average unused reserved GPU-minutes delta per pool within 15% of baseline (avoid new waste).
- Ensure predictable billing: soft-bursts billed at a transparent premium and visible in Console within 10s of allocation.
- Time to reclaim a soft-burst lease under emergency reclaim < 60s.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for long-term capacity commitments or contractual SLAs.
- Not intended to run model training or long-running batch jobs in Spectator Lanes.

High-level flow:
1) Spectator continuously aggregates signals: per-tenant QPS, token rates, tail latency, KV cache reuse, GPU utilization, temperature/thermal headroom, and recent allocation churn.
2) Spectator computes a demand intensity score and a confidence band (probabilistic short-term forecast).
3) When confidence band indicates a transient spike that is likely to be absorbed (< 30 minutes), Spectator emits a proposal to Autoscale Broker: {tenant, delta-cpu/gpu, duration-minutes, expected-cost, risk-score}.
4) Broker runs a fast viability check: checks cross-pool soft budgets, tenant billing/credit status, isolation constraints, and active fallbacks. If accepted, Broker allocates a soft-burst lease and tags the runtime with metadata (lease-id, expiry, billing-code).
5) If pool slack disappears or risk threshold exceeded, Broker revokes or throttles the lease and executes the preconfigured Fallback Contract for the tenant.

Autoscaler heuristics (prototype rules):
- Min-sample window: 60s; Max-sample window: 15m for spike detection.
- Demand intensity combines moving-average QPS and exponential tail weights for P95/P99 token rates.
- Only propose bursts when (estimated marginal latency impact > threshold) AND (probability of spillback < 10%).
- Soft-burst delta capped by min(tenant-headroom*0.5, pool-freeable-capacity*0.25).
- Limit concurrent soft leases per pool to avoid cascade failure (config default: 8).

Isolation controls / safety fences:
- QoS tagging: all runtime lanes tagged as COMMITTED, SOFT-BURST, SPECTATOR. Kernel-level niceness and GPU stream priorities enforce lane isolation.
- Memory / KV cache caps per lane to prevent cross-tenant KV pollution. Eviction thresholds are enforced aggressively on SPECTATOR lanes.
- Billing and circuit-breaker: if the tenant's billing status is delinquent, autoscale proposals fail fast.
- Preemptive reclaim policy: if overall pool utilization > 90% for >30s, reclaim order: SPECTATOR -> SOFT-BURST (by risk descending) -> Opportunistic queued work.

Fallback contract examples (must be configurable per tenant):
- Variant downgrade: switch to quantized/low-fidelity model variant with guaranteed upper-bound latency (prefers deterministic quality degradation over latency spikes).
- Rate-smoothing: apply token-based pacing to match baseline QPS with exponential decay to clear backlog gracefully.
- Partial routing: route new requests to Hosted fallback or Dedicated-cold pool if latency budget exceeded.

Telemetry & observability requirements:
- Per-lease metrics: lease-granted, lease-revoked, lease-duration, revoked-reason, peak-utilization, reclaim-latency.
- Pool heatmaps: lane-level utilization (5s resolution), tail-latency contours, KV cache hit-rate by lane.
- Cost transparency: show estimated cost delta and realized cost for each soft-burst in Console billing UI.
- Alerts: automated alert when reclaimed-leases/sec > threshold or when reclaim-latency > 60s.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces that include lease-id so we can correlate client-side SLA violations to specific soft leases or reclaimed events.

Operational playbook (runbook snippets):
- Normal spike: Spectator issues proposal -> Broker grants -> Monitor for 10m -> If stable, decay lease duration (auto-extend up to policy). Communicate to tenant via Console notification.
- Sustained overload: If a tenant consumes > 15% of pool for > 1h despite being on soft-burst, auto-evict to fallback contract and open a support ticket (owner: Customer Success).
- Emergency reclaim: Ops can trigger global reclaim mode which immediately revokes SOFT-BURST and SPECTATOR lanes; a fast script sets Broker mode to "reclaim-all" and routes telemetry to incident channel.

Billing model (draft):
- Soft-bursts priced at a flat premium multiplier (e.g., 1.6x) on top of committed unit price for the lease minutes. Visibility must appear on the tenant usage card with line-item detail.
- Spectator lane compute costs absorbed by pool owner but visible as a separate internal chargeback for SRE metrics and optimization.

Compatibility and API shape (rough):
- Proposal: POST /v1/pools/{pool}/proposals {tenant_id, delta_gpu_units, duration_minutes, reason, priority_hint, signature} -> returns proposal_id and recommended_action.
- Lease management: POST /v1/pools/{pool}/leases {proposal_id} -> lease_id; DELETE /v1/pools/{pool}/leases/{lease_id} -> revoke
- Tenant config: PATCH /v1/tenants/{t}/fallbacks {fallback_profiles: [variant, rate_smooth, route_fallback], soft_burst_policy: {max_concurrency, max_delta}}

Security / compliance notes:
- Lease metadata must not leak tenant PII; use tenant_id mapping and audit logs for compliance.
- All actions by Broker must be auditable and signed by service identity for on-prem/private deployments.
- For Private deployments, Spectator can run in customer VPC but Broker must be installable as an operator that respects airgap constraints.

Prototype plan & experiment matrix (next 6 weeks):
Week 0-1: Lightweight Spectator PoC: aggregate metrics, compute demand score, create a dashboard.
Week 2: Autoscale Broker stub that accepts Spectator proposals but requires manual approval (semi-automated).
Week 3-4: Run controlled experiments in 2 pilot pools: enable auto-proposals but do not auto-grant (ops approval required). Collect telemetry and false-positive rate.
Week 5: Enable auto-grant with conservative caps (single soft lease per pool, cap 10% delta). Monitor and iterate.
Week 6: Introduce reclaim automation and build Console UX for lease visibility + billing line-item.

Open questions / risks (to triage):
- Pricing sensitivity: will customers accept soft-burst premium or prefer to buy more reserved? Need pricing experiments.
- Complexity of QoS enforcement across different GPU drivers and cloud providers; kernel-level isolation may behave differently.
- Risk of cascade reclaims: reclaiming many leases simultaneously may create a thundering herd; need randomized reclaim jitter.
- Observability heat: Spectator adds metric volume—cost of telemetry must be bounded.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Spike: implement Spectator demand score prototype (Ethan).
- [ ] Design: Broker API contract and authorization model (Marcus).
- [ ] SRE: identify cheap QoS knobs available across our supported infra (Sofia).
- [ ] PM: draft Console mockups for lease visibility and billing (Aisha).
- [ ] Legal: confirm that soft-burst billing language can be included in TOS addendum for pilot customers.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: Spectator is an observer-first pattern so we can iterate without immediate control-plane risk. The playbook emphasizes deterministic fallbacks over dynamic, unpredictable preemption.
- Feedback requested on the default reclaim order and the suggested caps; we should prioritize tenant SLO protection in our defaults.

Appendix: quick glossary (short)
- Committed lane: tenant capacity backed by reservation/commitment.
- Soft-burst: temporary, billable increase to soft quota.
- Spectator lane: best-effort, low-priority runtime lane used for opportunistic workloads.
